title: Refund Philosophy & Decision Framework
summary: Refunds are the exception, not the default.
body:
Refunds are the exception, not the default. Our responsibility is to deliver what we promise, support clients through uncertainty, and maintain clear boundaries.

When refunds may be considered

| Scenario | Standard outcome | Who decides |
|---|---|---|
| Program ascension (moving to higher tier) | Credit toward new program, not cash refund | CSD |
| Medical emergency or hospitalization | Review with empathy. Refund or credit possible. | CSD |
| Death in immediate family | Review with empathy. Refund or credit possible. | CSD |
| Major unforeseeable life event preventing participation | Review case by case. | CSD |
| Company failure to deliver access or key components | Refund or credit likely appropriate. | CSD |
| Material delivery failure for significant portion of paid period | Refund or credit likely appropriate. | CSD |
| Strategic / legal discretion (rare, leadership only) | One-time business decision. Not precedent. | Leadership only |

When refunds do not apply

| Situation | Correct response |
|---|---|
| Fear, doubt, or loss of confidence | Support conversation with coach |
| Dissatisfaction with pace of progress | Recovery is non-linear -- coaching adjustment |
| Non-participation, missed calls, lack of engagement | Re-engagement conversation |
| Financial regret or buyer's remorse (no extenuating event) | Not eligible |
| 'I changed my mind' | Not eligible unless within early cancellation window |

Legal threats

Legal language should not automatically trigger refunds. Steps:

Acknowledge receipt and pause before acting

Do not issue immediate refunds in response to threats

Separate emotional tone from actual legal risk

Escalate to leadership for review -- do not handle alone

What to say if a client threatens legal action:

"Thank you for reaching out. I want to make sure this is handled properly. I'm going to escalate this to our leadership team who will be in touch with you directly. I appreciate your patience."

title: Late Payment & Failed Payment Policy
summary: This process applies to all programs -- School, Academy, Platinum, Continuity, and Beyond Recovery.
body:
This process applies to all programs -- School, Academy, Platinum, Continuity, and Beyond Recovery.

| Week | Action | Owner | Access status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | Friendly outreach via email, Skool DM, or Discord DM. Assume good intent. | VA Team / Client Success | Full access maintained |
| Week 2 | Second manual outreach. Prompt resolution requested. | Client Success | Full access maintained |
| Week 3 | Final notice with 3-day deadline clearly stated. | Client Success | Full access maintained until deadline |
| Day of deadline (if unpaid) | Access paused -- community, coaching, and calls removed. | Operations | Access paused |
| Day 14+ (still unpaid) | Escalate to CSD. Treat as voluntary exit. | CSD | Access removed |

Week 1 message:

"Hey [name]! Just a quick note to let you know your recent membership payment didn't go through. When you get a moment, could you please update your payment method so we can keep your access uninterrupted? Thank you!"

Week 2 message:

"Hey [name], just following up regarding your outstanding membership payment. We haven't yet received confirmation that it's been resolved. To avoid any interruption in your access to coaching, calls, and the community, please update your payment details as soon as possible. Thank you!"

Week 3 final notice:

"Hey [name], to continue your membership and access to [Program Name] we require payment by [DATE -- 3 days from today]. If payment is not received by this deadline, community, coaching, and call access will be removed. Thank you!"

NOTE: If a client proactively contacts us about financial hardship before the Week 3 deadline, explore a short pause or payment arrangement before removing access. Proactive communication is respected. Silence is treated as withdrawal.

title: Coach Change Requests
summary: When a client requests a different coach:
body:
When a client requests a different coach:

Coach or client success acknowledges the request warmly, no defensive response.

Client Success reviews current coach capacity and available coaches.

If capacity allows: coordinate the transition by completn. Aim to complete within 7 business days.

The original coach writes a brief handover note covering: client history, current zone, what's working, what to watch for.

The new coach schedules an introductory call within 5 business days of assignment.

Log the change in the client roster with reason.

What to say to the client:

"Absolutely, we want to make sure you have the right support. Let me look at our team and find the best fit. I'll be back to you within [2 days] with who we're pairing you with."

title: Ascension Prorated Refund
summary: When a client ascends from one program to a higher-tier program mid-billing cycle, they receive a prorated refund for the unused portion of their current membership.
body:
When a client ascends from one program to a higher-tier program mid-billing cycle, they receive a prorated refund for the unused portion of their current membership. This replaces the previous practice of issuing full-month refunds at time of ascension.

Calculation:

Formula: (Monthly Price ÷ Days in Billing Cycle) × Remaining Days = Refund Amount

Please use this Refund Calculator as needed: https://cfsrecovery.co/prorated-refund-caculator

Example

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| Program | Recovery Academy ($297/mo) |
| Billing cycle | May 1 – May 31 (31 days) |
| Ascension date | May 15 |
| Days used | 14 (May 1–14) |
| Remaining days | 17 (May 15–31) |
| Refund | ($297 ÷ 31) × 17 = $162.87 |

Process

| Step | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Client confirms ascension. New program enrollment is completed. | Enrollment / Coach |
| 2 | Calculate the prorated refund using the formula above or the Prorated Refund Calculator. | Operations |
| 3 | Issue refund to original payment method within 5 business days. | Operations |
| 4 | Remove previous program access on ascension date. New program access begins immediately. | Operations |
| 5 | Log refund amount, calculation, and ascension details in client roster. | Operations |

NOTE: If the ascension happens on day 1 of the billing cycle (same day as payment), a full refund is issued. If it happens on the last day of the billing cycle, no refund is issued. CSD approval is required for all ascension refunds.

title: Unsigned Service Agreement
summary: All Platinum members are required to sign a Service Agreement before beginning the program.
body:
All Platinum members are required to sign a Service Agreement before beginning the program. This policy outlines the escalation process when a client does not respond within the expected timeframe.

| Step | Timing | Action | Sent by | Access status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Request 1 | Within 48 hours of enrollment | Service agreement sent via email with signing instructions. | Brent (Ops) | Active |
| Request 2 | 5 business days after Request 1 | Follow-up message via Discord or Skool DM. Friendly reminder. | Brent (Ops) | Active |
| Final Notice | 5 business days after Request 2 | Final notice from leadership. 3-day signing deadline clearly stated. | Miguel | Active until deadline |
| Deadline passed | 3 days after Final Notice | Membership paused. Access removed until agreement is signed. | Operations | Paused |
| 14+ days | 14 days after pause | Escalate to CSD. Treat as potential voluntary exit. | CSD | Removed |

Request 2 message (Brent):

“Hey [Name]! Just a quick follow-up.  I sent over your Service Agreement a few days ago and wanted to make sure it didn’t get lost in the shuffle. When you get a moment, could you take a look and get that signed? It’s just a standard part of getting everything set up for your Platinum experience. Let me know if you have any questions!”

Final notice message (Miguel):

“Hey [Name], hope you’re doing well! I wanted to reach out personally because we’ve sent the Platinum Service Agreement over a couple of times now and it looks like it hasn’t been signed yet. The Service Agreement is a required step for all Platinum members, and we do need it completed to keep your membership active. We need this signed by [DATE — 3 business days from today]. If we don’t receive it by then, we’ll need to pause your membership and access until it’s taken care of. If you have any questions about the agreement or want to hop on a quick call to go through it, I’m happy to do that. Just let me know!”

NOTE: Paused time does not extend the Platinum term. The membership clock continues. Once the agreement is signed, access is restored within 24 hours. If a client has questions or concerns about the agreement, offer to walk through it on a call. Do not pressure, just require. Log all outreach attempts and dates in the client roster.

NOTE: This policy mirrors the U2 Late Payment escalation structure: two friendly requests from Ops, then a leadership final notice with a clear deadline. The tone should remain warm throughout. The goal is compliance, not confrontation.

title: Coach Transition Policy & Process
summary: Platinum Program Only
body:
Platinum Program Only

### Policy Overview:

Every Platinum Thriver is assigned a main coach when they join Platinum, based on coach availability at the time of enrollment. As a Thriver's main coach, you are their primary point of contact and are responsible for tracking their overall progress and recovery journey.

Having a main coach doesn't restrict a Thriver from interacting with other coaches. Specialist coaches may still be brought in for specific calls or topics, and multiple coaches may occasionally be present in group settings. However, for accountability, load management, and consistency of care, every Platinum Thriver should have one clearly designated main coach at all times.

Key Rules:

This policy applies to the Platinum program only.

Each Thriver is allowed one coach transition total during their time in the program. Extenuating circumstances may allow for additional changes.

Ie. if we request the coach change, applicable life events.

A transition must be formally requested and approved, informal arrangements do not count as an official transition.

Multiple coaches being present in a chat does not change a Thriver's assigned main coach.

The Coach Transition Form is not publicly available. It lives internally on the Wiki and is only sent to a Thriver once a transition conversation has already taken place.

When To Think About a Coach Transition:

When an non-primary coach is being @’d more frequently then the main coach

If the non-primary coach has had 2 or more consecutive 1 on 1 calls with the Thriver

NOTE: This does not designate the need for a change, but are the signals if applicable.

There's a mismatch in coaching style or communication approach.

The Thriver has a specific need that aligns better with another coach's specialization.

The current coaching relationship isn't progressing effectively.

A coach's availability or capacity changes significantly.

Who Initiates the Conversation

Either you or the Thriver may initiate a transition conversation, but the preferred approach is for you, the coach, to initiate if you feel a transition would better serve the Thriver.

If a Thriver initiates the conversation, treat this as a potential red flag and note it internally. It may indicate a breakdown in the coaching relationship, unmet expectations, or a communication issue that warrants a closer look before proceeding. The client success team should have a brief internal conversation about the context before moving forward.

Coach Alignment Before Any Commitment

Before sending the form, promising anything, or agreeing to a transition with a Thriver, the coaches involved should always discuss the situation among themselves and contact the Client Success Director. No commitment, verbal or written, should be made to a Thriver or Client until this internal alignment has taken place. This ensures the decision is fully vetted and supported before the Thriver is given any expectation about the outcome.

The Form Formalizes, It Doesn't Start

In either case, the transition conversation should happen before the form is sent. The form is not a starting point, it's used to formalize a decision that has already been discussed.

title: Platinum Cohorts: Structure & Schedule
summary: Platinum is delivered through cohorts.
body:
Platinum is delivered through cohorts. There are currently three active cohorts. Start times are held consistent wherever possible so Enrollment can place incoming Thrivers correctly, so Thrivers can select their preferred time at sign-up, and to avoid Zoom-link issues.

| Cohort | Days | Times | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platinum A1 | Tuesdays, Fridays | 8AM PDT / 9AM MDT / 10AM CDT / 11AM EDT / 4PM BST / 5PM CEST | Typically kicks off the first Tuesday of the month |
| Platinum A2 | Mondays, Thursdays | Set with Enrollment | Typically kicks off mid-month; some flexibility depending on Enrollment |
| Platinum B | Tuesdays & Thursdays, or Tuesdays & Fridays | 5PM PDT / 6PM MDT / 7PM CDT / 8PM EDT / 8AM AWST / 10AM AEST | Typically kicks off the first Tuesday of the month |

Some flexibility on days and kickoffs is possible, but times are kept consistent wherever possible. Any change to a cohort’s days or times must be cleared with Enrollment and the CSD first, because of the downstream effects on sign-ups and scheduling.

title: Joining Multiple Cohorts
summary: If a Thriver asks to join more than one cohort, for scheduling reasons or otherwise, encourage them to choose the single cohort they can attend most consistently and use that as their group.
body:
If a Thriver asks to join more than one cohort, for scheduling reasons or otherwise, encourage them to choose the single cohort they can attend most consistently and use that as their group. Multiple-cohort participation has been allowed in the past, but Platinum works best when a Thriver builds consistency within one cohort: it creates continuity, strengthens the coaching relationship, and lets them fully engage with their group experience.

If a Thriver cannot attend a scheduled call, the coach leading their cohort posts the replay link in the Thriver’s chat so they stay up to date.

The Thriver can also ask questions in their chat and receive support from the coaching team there.

Principle - prioritise consistency and continuity within one cohort, using replays and chat support to bridge any missed calls.

title: Platinum Q&A Calls & Cohort Size
summary: Whether a cohort runs its own Platinum Q&A call depends on its active size, so that coaching resources are used efficiently while protecting the quality of the experience.
body:
Whether a cohort runs its own Platinum Q&A call depends on its active size, so that coaching resources are used efficiently while protecting the quality of the experience. This is especially relevant for Platinum B.

| Active cohort size | Q&A arrangement |
|---|---|
| 2 or fewer active Thrivers | No separate Platinum Q&A call is run. Those Thrivers attend the Academy call that best fits their schedule and time zone. |
| 3 or more active Thrivers | A dedicated Platinum Q&A call is scheduled and run for that cohort. |

Principle - dedicated Platinum Q&A calls are reserved for cohorts with enough participation to support meaningful group discussion. Smaller cohorts are supported through Academy calls, chat coaching, and call replays.

title: Cohort Coach, Preferences & Changing Coaches
summary: Each Thriver works primarily with the coach leading their cohort.
body:
Each Thriver works primarily with the coach leading their cohort. We see consistently better outcomes when Thrivers maintain continuity with their cohort coach, as it improves communication, accountability, and the overall coaching experience.

If a Thriver requests a specific coach, or will only join Platinum if they can work with a particular coach, a Meet-and-Greet call with that coach may be offered before the first four weeks of Platinum begin.

During the four-week cohort experience, Thrivers should be strongly encouraged to work primarily with the coach leading their chosen cohort.

Once the four-week cohort portion is complete, the Thriver may schedule future 1:1 calls with the coach of their choice.

This guideline covers coach preference and fit within the cohort. For a formal, ongoing change of a Thriver’s assigned main coach, follow Universal Policy U9 (Coach Transition Policy & Process).

title: Platinum Discord Chat & Coach Communication
summary: The coach leading a Thriver’s cohort serves as the Thriver’s primary point of contact within Discord.
body:
The coach leading a Thriver’s cohort serves as the Thriver’s primary point of contact within Discord.

If a Thriver would like input from another coach, they may tag that coach directly using the @ symbol, ensuring the coach’s name highlights correctly. This notifies the coach that their support or perspective is being requested on a specific question.

In rare circumstances, another coach may be approved to take the lead in a Thriver’s chat. This should happen only when there is a clear, compelling reason and must have prior approval from Leadership/CSD. Wherever possible, continuity with the cohort coach is maintained.

Principle - maintain one clear primary coaching relationship and prioritise continuity, while allowing additional coaching support when requested and approved exceptions when warranted. Frequent tagging of a non-primary coach can be a signal to consider a transition (see Universal Policy U9).

title: Rejoining or Repeating a Platinum Cohort
summary: This covers two situations:
body:
This covers two situations: a Thriver who missed part of a cohort for legitimate reasons and needs to rejoin, and a Thriver who completed (or largely completed) the cohort and would like to repeat the first four weeks for additional reinforcement.

Rejoining (missed content)

In rare circumstances a Thriver may need to withdraw from or miss part of the Platinum cohort due to unforeseen life events, health challenges, or scheduling conflicts. In these cases they may be permitted to rejoin and complete the first four weeks with a future cohort.

The Thriver’s primary coach remains unchanged and continues to own the client record (CLU). The Thriver’s Discord chat may be temporarily moved under the active cohort so the coach leading that cohort can easily share call links, replays, and other cohort communications.

Repeating (reinforcement)

If a Thriver did not have a significant reason for missing the content but later wishes to take part in the first four weeks again, repeating the cohort may be offered as an exception for an additional fee.

As of June 9, 2026, the cost to repeat the first four weeks of the Platinum cohort is $750 USD. This pricing is subject to change at any time, and does not include any additional one-on-one calls.

Approval for rejoining or repeating a cohort is reviewed case-by-case. Principle - preserve coaching continuity with the primary coach while providing reasonable pathways for Thrivers to access missed content or repeat the cohort experience when appropriate.

title: Overview & Scope
summary: The Caregiver Add-On gives a Platinum Thriver’s caregiver their own supported relationship with CFS Recovery:
body:
The Caregiver Add-On gives a Platinum Thriver’s caregiver their own supported relationship with CFS Recovery: a dedicated Discord chat managed by the Thriver’s coach, caregiver-specific education, and a weekly group call. It makes explicit the support coaches have been delivering informally, defines its boundaries, and ensures the coach’s workload is properly reflected and paid for.

What it is not

Not a standalone product. It is only available attached to a Platinum membership.

Not therapy or counselling for the caregiver.

Not an emergency or crisis service.

Not a mediation service for family conflict.
sourceNote: Master Program Policy v3.6 · Caregiver Add-On

One caregiver per Thriver. The family designates a single person (for example, mom or dad). Extenuating circumstances are handled as a documented policy exception with CSD approval.

Best fit: Thrivers whose recovery depends heavily on a family member who controls pacing, household load, or day-to-day decisions.

A caregiver is required for Thrivers who are unable to join calls themselves due to capacity, and for minors under the age of 16.

title: Chat Rules & Coach Boundaries
summary: These three rules define the scope of the caregiver relationship.
body:
These three rules define the scope of the caregiver relationship. They protect the coach from being pulled into family mediation, and should be reflected in the Discord guideline doc and the coach SOP.

| Rule | What it means in practice |
|---|---|
| Anchored to recovery | Every caregiver conversation stays focused on the Thriver’s recovery. Recovery is the subject of the chat, not the relationship and not the caregiver’s own treatment. |
| Not an emergency hotline | The chat is governed by the Discord guideline doc. Crisis situations route out of the chat, not into it. |
| Confidentiality with limits | What is said in each chat stays in that chat, unless withholding it would harm the Thriver’s recovery or there is a safety concern. |
sourceNote: Master Program Policy v3.6 · Caregiver Add-On

title: How It Works Operationally
summary: Coach capacity & CLUs
body:
Coach capacity & CLUs

Each caregiver counts as 1.0 CLU. All caregivers and caregiver clients start at 1.0.

No separate caregiver cap. Caregivers are carried like standard CLUs, based on what each coach chooses to hold.

Chat structure

One caregiver chat per Thriver, held by the Thriver’s own coach.

The coach therefore runs both sides, the Thriver’s chat and the caregiver’s chat, under the confidentiality rule in CG4.

Call cadence

The weekly caregiver group call is the standard rhythm.

Month one includes the 30-minute 1-on-1 onboarding call.

After that, individual check-ins are monthly or as-needed, at coach discretion.

The caregiver chat mirrors the Thriver chat on response time and cadence.

Existing caregivers

Grandfathered in at no additional cost. Their service does not change and they do not receive the new calls. If they would like the full package, they can purchase it.

They still count as 1.0 CLU each for coach load purposes.

Roster reflection is being handled in a dedicated working session.

title: Who Qualifies (Readiness Gate)
summary: Beyond Recovery is a personal development program for people who have genuinely recovered.
body:
Beyond Recovery is a personal development program for people who have genuinely recovered. It is not a continuation of recovery coaching. Access requires a qualifying conversation every time, regardless of which program the member is coming from.

Readiness Criteria All four must be true before access is granted:

Symptoms are not driving daily decisions

Not regularly attending recovery-focused calls or coaching

Clearly understands Beyond Recovery is personal development, not continued recovery coaching

Energized about building their full life, not just relieved to be done with recovery

If even one of these is missing, the right answer is continued support, not Beyond Recovery.

Access by Program:

| Where They Are | Qualifying Call | Who Runs It | Free Trial |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active Platinum | Yes, Next Steps Call | Their coach | 14 days |
| Active Continuity | Yes, check-in or Next Steps Call | Their coach | 14 days |
| Lapsed Platinum or Continuity | Yes, standalone call | Their former coach or Junior | 14 days |
| Active Academy or School | Yes, standalone call | Junior | 14 days |
| Lapsed Academy or School | Yes, standalone call | Junior | 14 days |
| No prior membership | Yes, standalone call | Junior | No trial, full price |

Junior handles all trial activations and any qualifying call where there is no existing coach relationship. Coach judgment takes precedence over client preference when it comes to readiness.

### Quick Answers for Common Situations

Client pushing for Beyond but coach is not sure they are ready:

Default to Continuity. Easier to move them forward later than pull them back after a poor Beyond experience.

Academy or School member asking about Beyond without booking a call:

Direct them to book a call with Junior. No details about Beyond until the call happens.

Lapsed Platinum member wants Beyond:

They get the 14-day trial after Junior's call confirms readiness.

Coach unsure between Platinum and Beyond for an Academy member:

Flag it. Junior and the coaching team decide together.
sourceNote: Master Program Policy v3.6 · Beyond Recovery

title: 14 Day Free Trial
summary: The 14-day free trial is a benefit tied to having been a Platinum or Continuity member.
body:
The 14-day free trial is a benefit tied to having been a Platinum or Continuity member. Active status at the time of the request is not required. A member who completed Platinum, took time away, and later wants to explore Beyond Recovery is still eligible for the trial provided they pass the qualifying call.

Academy and School members are not eligible for the free trial. Junior answers their questions during the qualifying call, which serves as their preview of the program.

Trials are activated by Junior after the qualifying call confirms readiness. Trials are a one-time offer and cannot be re-extended.

How to offer the free trial:

"You've worked incredibly hard over these last [X] months. As a thank you, we'd like to give you your first month in Beyond Recovery on us, no obligation, just a chance to experience it and see if it resonates with where you're headed."
sourceNote: Master Program Policy v3.6 · Beyond Recovery
